svg.title: Polarization of a dielectric in a capacitor
svg.desc: (a) Between a plate with charge +Q on the left and a plate with −Q on the right, the molecules of the dielectric are polarized: each oval molecule has its negative end toward the positive plate and its positive end toward the negative plate. The result is a layer of negative charge on the dielectric surface facing the positive plate and positive charge on the surface facing the negative plate. (b) Field lines leave the +Q plate. Some cross the whole gap; the others end on the negative surface charge of the dielectric, and matching lines start again on its positive surface charge and end on the −Q plate. Fewer lines cross the dielectric, so the field inside it is weaker.
